answer.why_different: The generated document appears to confuse the callback URI variable `notificationTarget` with the request-body property that supplies its value, `notificationRecipientAddress`. It also emits both a non-runtime-expression callback key and a separate runtime-expression key, creating a structural duplicate instead of one callback address.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification defines the callback resource URI variable as `notificationTarget`, whose value is the notification recipient address identified by `notificationRecipientAddress`. It also requires POST notifications to use that target and to support 204 and 4xx/5xx responses.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI callback keys must be runtime expressions enclosed in braces, and a request-body property is referenced using syntax such as `$request.body#/property`. Therefore `{notificationTarget}` is not a valid runtime expression, while `$request.body#/notificationTarget` refers to a different request-body property than the one identified by the specification.
answer.clearer_why: The official side presents one callback keyed by the recipient-address expression. The generated side presents two callback entries, one invalid as a runtime expression and one pointing at the wrong property, which is more confusing even though its intent is partly explicit.

differences.reason: The generated side omits the callback keyed by the recipient-address reference, so it does not preserve the callback address represented on the official side. The specification links `notificationTarget` to `notificationRecipientAddress` (S7), and the official context contains that callback key (C1).

`{notificationTarget}` is an extra callback key and is not a valid OpenAPI runtime expression: callback keys must identify a runtime expression (O4), whose syntax uses forms such as `$request.body#/...` (O3). The specification names `notificationTarget` as a URI variable, not as a standalone runtime expression (S7).

Although `$request.body#/notificationTarget` has runtime-expression form, it references `notificationTarget` in the request body rather than the specified `notificationRecipientAddress`; S7 identifies the latter as the address contained in the subscription. It therefore creates a callback at a different address from the official one (C1, C2, S7).

#### Callback Object  
A map of possible out-of band callbacks related to the parent operation.
Each value in the map is a [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) that describes a set of requests that may be initiated by the API provider and the expected responses.
The key value used to identify the callback object is an expression, evaluated at runtime, that identifies a URL to use for the callback operation.  
##### Patterned Fields
Field Pattern | Type | Description
---|:---:|---

UserRepositories:
# returns array of '#/components/schemas/repository'
operationRef: 'https://na2.gigantic-server.com/#/paths/~12.0~1repositories~1{username}/get'
parameters:
username: $response.body#/username
```  
Note that in the use of `operationRef`, the _escaped forward-slash_ is necessary when
using JSON references.  
##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name

evidence.query: callback runtime expression URL of the notification request body {request.body#/notificationRecipientAddress} {notificationTarget} $request.body#/notificationTarget
evidence.title: Examples
evidence.text:
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)
```  
The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
